extension_metadata.note: Stress-test #7 finding: NYU publishes a full, itemized Cost of Attendance rather than a single tuition figure. Direct/billed items (tuition, health insurance, books, food, housing -- the latter two billed because on-campus housing is guaranteed for all 4 years) are captured as mandatory_fees_breakdown; non-billed planning estimates (transportation, personal expenses) are captured as estimated_living_costs_annual. Total of tuition_annual + mandatory_fees_annual + estimated_living_costs_annual = 68576 + 15838 + 5914 = 90328, matching NYU's own published 'Total Estimated Cost of Attendance: $90,328' exactly -- no EvidaPath-derived total was needed beyond the schema's own canonical fields, unlike TUM which required a second CostProfile record. Stress-test #10 finding: this single CostProfile record serves ALL applicants uniformly -- no UAE-national/non-UAE-national or domestic/international sticker-cost tier was found published. No blocked-account or visa proof-of-funds deposit requirement was found for UAE student visas in this run's research (see missing-data.json) -- this is a genuine structural difference from TUM's German blocked-account requirement, not yet independently confirmed absent by a UAE government immigration source, so it is NOT recorded as a VERIFIED ABSENCE here, only as an unresearched gap.

source_records.excerpt: Applicants use the Common Application, select New York University, and then have the option to be considered at one of our three degree-granting campuses: Abu Dhabi, New York City, or Shanghai (with the option to list up to two alternates). However, you'll only receive one admissions decision from NYU. Required materials: Common Application form, USD $85 application fee (waivers available), school report and official transcript, one letter of recommendation, STARS (Self-Reported Transcript and Academic Record System), NYU Abu Dhabi Applicant Profile, English proficiency test (for non-native speakers, with limited exceptions), standardized test scores (optional through 2027-2028 cycle), optional essay on bridge-building. Select applicants will be invited to participate in the NYU Abu Dhabi Candidate Weekend, the final evaluative component in the admissions process. References apply through the 2027-2028 application cycle.
source_records.notes: Primary official NYUAD applicant-facing apply page. Confirms university-wide Common Application with campus preference rather than direct NYUAD-only application, and existence of Candidate Weekend as final evaluative step.
source_records.title: Apply for Admission - NYU Abu Dhabi

source_records.excerpt: NYU will remain test-optional through the 2027-2028 application cycle. Applicants are not required to submit standardized test scores. Results from standardized testing exams are an important criteria for evaluating our global pool of applicants. NYU maintains one of the most flexible testing policies of any college or university. Non-native English speakers must generally submit proficiency exam results from within two years prior, unless they have studied in English-only curricula for three consecutive years before applying. In general, most students for whom English is not their first language can expect to submit English language testing, even if they have been in a fully English-speaking curriculum. No specific curriculum requirements are listed; applicants come from a wide range of educational systems and backgrounds. Applicants must be 17 years old by August 1 of the year they plan to enroll.
source_records.notes: Primary official NYUAD entry-requirements page. Explicit basis for the VERIFIED-ABSENCE claim that no curriculum-specific academic cutoff is published, and for test-optional / English-proficiency policy.
source_records.title: Entry Requirements - NYU Abu Dhabi

source_records.excerpt: Computer Science Major. The program requires quantitative coursework, including at least one semester of calculus. Applicants are encouraged to have a strong foundation in algebra, pre-calculus, and/or calculus and related core mathematical skills. A Computer Science Minor is also available as an alternative option.
source_records.notes: Primary NYUAD program-marketing page for Computer Science. Degree type (BS) and CIP code not stated here; confirmed instead via the NYU Bulletins program page (src-04).
source_records.title: Computer Science Major - NYU Abu Dhabi

source_records.excerpt: Computer Science (BS). CIP: 11.0701. Program aims to train students both in the fundamental principles of computer science and in related aspects of technology. Computer Science majors must complete a minor or major in one of: Applied Mathematics, Economics, Engineering, Interactive Media, Natural Sciences, or Sound and Music Computing. Total Credits: 128. Major Requirements: 54 credits minimum. Required Minor: 16 credits. General Education: 26 credits. General Electives: 32 credits. Core major courses include Introduction to Computer Science, Discrete Mathematics, Data Structures, Algorithms, Computer Systems Organization, Research Seminar, and Capstone Project.
source_records.notes: Authoritative NYU Bulletins catalog entry -- the canonical source for the exact official degree title 'Computer Science (BS)', confirming it is NOT labeled 'Computer Science' alone or 'BA in Computer Science'. Also the source for the unusual required-second-credential structural rule.

source_records.excerpt: Applications use the Common Application. Early Decision I: Deadline November 1; Decision December 15 (binding). Early Decision II: Deadline January 1; Decision February 15 (binding). Regular Decision: Deadline January 5; Decision April 1 (non-binding). NYU has extended the test-optional policy for the 2026-2027 cycle. NYU Abu Dhabi is not accepting applications for transfer students in the 2026-27 admissions cycle. Admissions criteria focus on academic excellence, extracurricular activities, teacher and counselor evaluations, and a demonstrated interest in global citizenship, service, and leadership.

source_records.excerpt: Every admitted student is considered for limited merit-based support. Need-based aid available for those demonstrating financial need via CSS Profile. All NYUAD applicants are encouraged to file the CSS Profile. Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed NYUAD Scholarship for Exceptional Emirati Students, funded by Abu Dhabi government, for all admitted UAE nationals and children of an Emirati mother or father. Falcon Dirhams (Personal Support Award) for UAE national students demonstrating financial need via CSS Profile. All financial aid grants offered by NYUAD for non-Emirati citizens are based on financial need. Your combined awards from all sources cannot exceed the estimated annual Cost of Attendance.

source_records.excerpt: Students must declare a major by the end of their second year, though some majors do have requirements beginning in the first year. To earn a degree, students must fulfill: a minimum of 128 credits (32 full courses) with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0; a First-Year Writing Seminar; the Core Curriculum across four areas of inquiry; requirements for an academic major; two January Term courses; a Capstone project. A Bachelor of Arts is typically awarded to students in Arts and Humanities, Social Science, or Psychology majors, while a BS degree is awarded to students who major in Engineering or Science.
source_records.notes: Primary NYUAD official governance page. States major-declaration deadline as 'end of their second year' -- compare src-09, which states 'spring break of their second year' on the same topic from a different official NYU source. Logged as a genuine cross-source conflict, not resolved by guessing.
source_records.title: Graduation Requirements for Undergraduates - NYU Abu Dhabi

source_records.excerpt: Students declare a major by spring break of their second year. All final updates to major, minor, core requirements must be submitted by the student no later than the end of add/drop of the final spring or fall semester of enrollment. Grades of C or higher are earned count toward major, minor, or Core requirements. NYU Abu Dhabi offers 26 undergraduate majors across various divisions. No competitive admission process, caps, or GPA requirements to declare or enter specific majors (including Computer Science) are stated.
source_records.notes: Registrar bulletin, states 'spring break of their second year' -- conflicts with src-08's 'end of their second year'. Also the basis for the verified-absence claim that Computer Science major entry has no published competitive cap or GPA gate distinct from ordinary graduation GPA (2.0 minimum, C-or-higher-counts rule).

source_records.title: Academic Policies | NYU Bulletins (Abu Dhabi)

source_records.excerpt: Financial support is individualized based on demonstrated need, not a fixed award. Award amounts vary depending on the student's financial need as determined by NYU's Office of Financial Aid. Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed NYUAD Scholarship for Exceptional Emirati Students -- eligibility: all admitted UAE nationals and children of an Emirati mother or father; awarded annually; does not require separate application. Falcon Dirhams (Personal Support Award) -- eligibility: UAE national students demonstrating financial need; requires CSS Profile submission.
source_records.notes: Corroborates src-06 on the two UAE-national-specific award mechanisms and explicitly states general aid is individualized/need-based rather than fixed.
source_records.title: Scholarships and Financial Aid - NYU Abu Dhabi

source_records.excerpt: All admitted Emirati students and children of Emirati mothers are awarded the Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed NYUAD Scholarship, which provides 100 percent financial coverage for tuition, registration fees, and study- and travel-related expenses for all four years. Every admitted student is considered for limited merit-based aid. NYUAD offers financial assistance to students who demonstrate financial need based on the results of the CSS Profile to all admitted students.
source_records.notes: The single clearest statement of the Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Scholarship's fixed, 100%-coverage scope -- the basis for modeling it as a genuine Scholarship record with award_type full_tuition rather than a personalized aid package.
source_records.title: UAE Applicants - NYU Abu Dhabi

source_records.excerpt: Accepted exams: TOEFL iBT, Duolingo English Test, IELTS Academic, PTE Academic, C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency (Cambridge English), iTEP. We don't have minimum score requirements, but competitive applicants will receive: TOEFL iBT 100+; Duolingo 130+; IELTS Academic 7.5+; PTE Academic 70+; Cambridge English Scale 191+; iTEP 4.5+. Testing is not required if English is your first language, or if you have already completed three or more consecutive academic years in a curriculum where the only language of instruction was English.
